1001060.etyen: Borrowed from English Miranda (“Miranda, California”). The English place name was applied to the local post office on 26 August 1905, replacing the earlier local name Jacobsen's Valley. The deeper origin of Miranda is uncertain. One historical account leaves open whether the intended reference was a female personal name or the well-known Spanish place and family name, while another credits Etta Coombs with choosing the name for the post office.

en.g: a male given name from Old Norse

1001316.etyen:
Inherited from Old Norse Sveinungr m. The Old Norse name was formed from Sveinn (“male given name; originally boy, young man, servant”) + -ungr (“kinship- or descendant-forming suffix”), and meant “kinsman or descendant of Svein” or “son of Svein”. The suffix -ungr does not represent the adjective ungr (“young”) in this name. Sveinn was itself originally a byname derived from sveinn (“boy, young man, servant”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk Sveinung, Faroese Sveinungur, Swedish Svenung and Svennung, and Danish Svenning (“male given name”).

1004644.etyen:
From the officially standardized Norwegian place-name element Trifan-, representing a local adaptation of Russian Трифон (Trifon), from Ancient Greek Τρύφων (Trúphōn, “delicate; one who lives softly or luxuriously”), ultimately from Ancient Greek τρυφάω (trupháō, “to live softly or luxuriously”), itself from Ancient Greek τρυφή (truphḗ, “softness, delicacy; luxury”), and the definite singular of nes (“headland, promontory”). The name refers to Saint Tryphon of Pechenga.
Compare Kven Triffananniemi and Northern Sami Triffannjárga, the Kven and Northern Sami names of the same headland, respectiv

en.g: block day; a school day on which the ordinary timetable is replaced by one or a small number of subjects taught in long consecutive blocks, typically with one subject occupying most or all of the day
x: På fredag har klassen blokkdag i fysikk og kan arbeide med laboratorieforsøk hele dagen.
On Friday, the class has a block day in physics and can work on laboratory experiments all day.
Har blokkdag i fysikk i morgen, og en av tingene vi skal gjøre er å putte forskjellige ting i en mikrobølgeovn for å se hva som skjer.
I have a block day in physics tomorrow, and one of the things we are going to do is put various things in a microwave oven to see what happens.

1004900.etyen:
From blokk (“block”) + dag (“day”), literally “block day”.
The first element, blokk (“block”), is from Middle Low German block (“block”). Here it is used in the abstract sense of a coherent or continuous unit, referring to ordinary teaching periods being grouped into longer blocks. Compare blokkundervisning (“block teaching, block instruction”). The second element, dag (“day”), is inherited from Old Norse dagr (“day”), and is related to døgn (“24-hour period”).
Compare the parallel formations Norwegian Nynorsk blokkdag and Danish blokdag (“block day”).
